name: libftdi
desc: Library to talk to FTDI chips
why: Talking to FTDI chips opens a real door into USB serial hardware, though it is mostly a library.

brief.what_it_is: libFTDI is an open source C library for talking to FTDI USB-serial chips, including the FT230X, FT4232H/FT2232H, FT232R/FT245R, FT2232L/D/C, FT232BM/FT245BM and FT8U232AM/FT8U245AM families. Your program links against it and gets access to the chip's USB interface, including bitbang mode. It takes USB device handles and data from your program and sends and receives bytes to and from the chip. The homepage also describes an ftdi_eeprom tool for reading and writing the chip's EEPROM configuration, which the brew metadata lists as an executable.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as an FTDI USB driver with bitbang mode for userspace programs, so developers can use FTDI hardware without writing a kernel driver. The page does not state a broader motivation.
brief.how_it_works: The library runs in userspace and is linked into your program, so no kernel driver is needed. It uses libusb as the USB layer, which the page says covers Linux, Windows, macOS and BSD. The 1.5 release notes add kernel driver auto attach/detach for the sio module, controlled by an AUTO_DETACH_REATACH_SIO_MODULE option.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no install steps beyond the brew formula. It does say libusb is the USB layer that makes Linux, Windows, macOS and BSD work. The 1.5 notes mention a build option named AUTO_DETACH_REATACH_SIO_MODULE, and the notes say old ftdi_usb_purge_* calls now produce deprecation warnings at compile time. I did not read the documentation or repository pages, so build details are unverified.
brief.standout: It is a userspace library with no kernel driver, which makes FTDI hardware reachable from ordinary programs, and it covers bitbang mode on a wide range of FTDI chips. The EEPROM programmer is a separate tool bundled alongside the library.
brief.status: quiet. The newest release on the homepage is version 1.5, dated 2020-07-07. The 1.4 and 1.3 entries are from 2017 and 2016. I could not see a last commit date, so I cannot say whether it is still actively maintained.
brief.caveats: The library is LGPL 2.1 (not any later version) and the EEPROM programmer is GPL 2 (not any later version), so the two parts have different licences. Only the chip families listed on the homepage are covered. Version 1.5 deprecated the ftdi_usb_purge_rx_buffer, ftdi_usb_purge_tx_buffer and ftdi_usb_purge_buffers functions in favour of ftdi_tc[io]flush. This is mainly a C library, so there is no end-user command-line experience to show. My notes come from the homepage only.
quotes: libFTDI is an open source library to talk to FTDI chips:
The library is linked with your program in userspace, no kernel driver required.
libFTDI works perfectly with Linux, Windows, MacOS X and BSD variants thanks to libusb.
